---
title: "Drafting the SPEC with an AI agent"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

> tflplanner is experimental: the screens and functions may change. This
> article follows the screens of the development version (`next`).

The **AI drafts** tab hands the study's materials (the TOC, the annotated
shells, the ADaM, the ADaM spec, the SAP) to an AI agent in your editor. The
agent writes a draft SPEC for each report and asks in its chat where the
materials do not settle a decision. tflplanner checks the drafts, copies the
ones you choose into the study, and makes the reports from them.

This article walks through the flow with the **AI sample**: a fictional study
(DMY-001, Example Pharma) with eight reports, made in one click. Everything in
it is fictional, and it holds no answers: the agent writes the SPEC.
The Japanese edition is [AI 連携の使い方](ja-ai-flow.html).

## What you need

- R 4.1 or later.
- An editor with an AI agent in **agent mode**, one of:
  - VS Code with GitHub Copilot (agent mode in its chat), or
  - Claude Code.
- A model of the strongest tier: see [Which model](#models).
- The tflplanner home **inside a folder the editor can open**. The agent
  reads only the study's `ai/` folder, which the editor opens as a folder.

## 1. Install and set up (once)

```{r}
install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("ichirio/rtfreporter@<tag>", upgrade = "never")
remotes::install_github("ichirio/tflspec@<tag>", upgrade = "never")
remotes::install_github("ichirio/tflplanner@<tag>", upgrade = "never")
# what the sample's reports use
install.packages(c("haven", "readxl", "officer", "cards", "cardx", "dplyr", "tidyr",
                   "ggsurvfit", "patchwork", "broom", "broom.helpers", "parameters"))

tflplanner::setup_tflplanner(home = "C:/work/tflplanner-home", language = "en")
tflplanner::add_shortcut()   # a desktop shortcut that starts the app
```

Use the tag you were given (or `next` for the development version). Start
the app with the shortcut or `tflplanner::run_app()`.

## 2. Make the study from the AI sample

1. On the **Studies** tab, press **New study...** (with no study yet, the
   start page has **The sample for the AI tab...**).
2. Under **Start from**, choose **The sample for the AI tab**.
3. Keep the study ID (`DMY-001`) or type your own, and press **Create**.

The study is made at once, in `studies/<ID>` under the home, and opened:

| Where | What |
|---|---|
| `docs/toc.xlsx` | The TOC (8 reports) |
| `docs/shells.xlsx` | The annotated shells (6 sheets, one shell a sheet) |
| `docs/adam_spec.xlsx` | The ADaM spec (Pinnacle 21 form) |
| `data/adam/` | 5 ADaM datasets (adsl, adae, adlb, advs, adtte) |
| `ai/docs/sap.docx` | The SAP, as a reference for the agent |

The materials leave some decisions open on purpose, to see whether the agent
asks instead of deciding silently.

## 3. Step 1: Write the prompt

The **AI drafts** tab opens on **1 Write the prompt**, with **The open study**
chosen and the fields filled: the TOC / SHELL workbook, the shell workbooks,
the ADaM folder (it says "5 files" under it), the ADaM spec, and `sap.docx`
under **Add a reference**. Each **Browse...** opens in the study's folder.

1. Press **Read and check**. The right side shows what was read: 8 TOC items,
   6 shells, the ADaM summary sent to the agent, and the workbook's sheets.
2. In **Sheets**, move `General conventions` (rules common to every report) to
   **Other sheets (not shells)** and press **Apply and read again**; then
   choose it in **Sheets for every request** on the left, so every request
   carries it.
3. Press **Write the requests**. The requests and the agent's prompt are
   written into the study's `ai/` folder.

## 4. Step 2: The agent writes the SPEC

1. On **2 The agent writes the SPEC**, press **Copy the prompt**.
2. Open the study's **`ai` folder** in the editor (`studies/DMY-001/ai`; in VS
   Code, double-clicking `ai/DMY-001.code-workspace` does the same). Do not
   open the study folder or `studies/` above it.
3. Put the chat in agent mode, paste the prompt and send it.

The agent works request by request. It writes its drafts into
`ai/spec/outputs/`, and its decisions into `ai/decisions.md`. Where the
materials do not settle something, it writes to you, in one numbered message
for each request:

- **It decides** where the TOC, the shells, the SAP and the ADaM spec agree.
  It records the decision as an assumption on the draft.
- **It asks you to confirm a default** where the materials disagree, for
  example a TOC that names one analysis set and the SAP another. Each
  question gives the report, what each document says (sheet, section), the
  default it would take and why, and the other choices.
- **It asks** where nothing in the materials answers, still with a default.

Answer in the chat, briefly ("1: FAS, 2: the raw data's digits + 1"). If it
stops, send "continue". If it starts installing packages or searching folders,
send "Follow AGENTS.md: only write the drafts."

## 5. Step 3: Check the SPEC

On **3 Check the SPEC**, press **Check** (you can press it while the agent is
still working). Each draft gets:

- **ERROR**: the SPEC does not read; it cannot be copied.
- **WARNING**: it reads, but no program can be made from it yet.
- **OK**: a program can be made.

For an ERROR or a WARNING, copy the fix text on its row, paste it into the
same chat, and check again once the agent has fixed it.

## 6. Step 4: Copy into the study, and make the reports

1. On **4 Copy into the study**, tick the reports to take (at first, the
   drafts not adopted yet are ticked) and press **Adopt (copy) the reports
   ticked into the study**. They go onto the study's Report list.
2. Where the agent assumed something, its assumptions and the points **to
   confirm** are listed with each report. Mark each as right or wrong; what is
   wrong can be sent back to the chat as a correction request.
3. Make the reports (the **Runs** tab, **Run all**) and open the RTFs.

## Which model {#models}

From a comparison on this sample (8 reports; the two hardest requests run
three times each; the same answers given in every run):

- **Use Opus or Fable.** Their results were equal within the noise of three
  runs: the same questions, defaults that agreed with the SAP and the define,
  no silent wrong decision, and the kit's rules kept. Choose between them by
  cost.
- **Sonnet and Haiku are not recommended** with the current kit. Sonnet chose
  a derivation wrongly in two runs of three (once silently, once as a wrong
  default), and rewrote requests whose drafts were already done. Haiku asked
  good questions, but repaired failed drafts by guessing, and its questions
  seldom said how the answer changes the numbers or why the default.
- **The editor made no difference** where it was tested: Fable gave the same
  result in VS Code with GitHub Copilot and in Claude Code (the same
  questions, all 8 reports made at the first try). Opus was tested in Claude
  Code only; the same is expected in Copilot, but it is not tested yet.

## What to expect of the drafts

- The drafts are **drafts**: a programmer reviews (QCs) every adopted report,
  as for one written by hand. The agent works from the materials it is given;
  where they are wrong or silent, so may the draft be.
- What the agent decided is never hidden: its assumptions and the points to
  confirm are on each report in step 4, and in `ai/decisions.md`. Read them
  first: they are where a draft is most likely to differ from what you meant.
- Some reports need a fix or two before they check OK; the shift tables were
  the hardest for every model.
